how_to_obtain.command: kubectl debug -it node/<node-name> --image=nicolaka/netshoot -- tcpdump -i any -n port <backend-service-port> -w /tmp/backend-capture.pcap && tcpdump -r /tmp/backend-capture.pcap -A | grep -E 'HTTP/|GET |POST |TLS|ClientHello'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS ClientHello/ServerHello handshake records visible in capture confirm encrypted backend connection. Plaintext HTTP verbs (GET, POST, HTTP/1.1) confirm absence of re-encryption.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the HAProxy Stats dashboard or Traefik dashboard, navigate to the backend server pool configuration and verify the server entries use HTTPS scheme or have SSL verification enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: HAProxy Stats UI → Backend Pools → Select Pool → Server List → Check 'SSL' column | Traefik Dashboard → HTTP → Backends → Verify scheme is https://
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server entries showing SSL/TLS enabled status or HTTPS scheme confirm backend re-encryption is active.

typical_values: false (common in clusters where ingress terminates TLS and forwards plaintext to ClusterIP services)
true (security-hardened deployments using HTTPS backends or service mesh with mTLS sidecar re-encryption)
null (unknown; common when proxy configuration has not been formally reviewed)

option_description: Describes whether the terminating proxy serves workloads from a single trust boundary (single namespace, security zone, or tenant) or is shared across multiple distinct trust boundaries such as different security zones, Kubernetes namespaces with different sensitivity classifications, or multi-tenant environments. A shared proxy creates a co-tenancy risk at the TLS termination point.
security_impact: The Rego rule tls_termination_at_shared_proxy fires when proxy_trust_boundary_scope is shared_across_trust_boundaries and tls_reencryption_to_backend_enabled is false, and also fires independently when the value is unknown without re-encryption. A shared proxy that terminates TLS from multiple security zones holds decrypted traffic from all tenants simultaneously, meaning a compromise of the proxy process exposes cross-boundary traffic. This enables asymmetric cryptography key exposure (T1573.002) and protocol tunneling for data exfiltration (T1572). The unknown state is treated as potentially risky because unreviewed proxy scope cannot be assumed safe.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Identify which namespaces and services route through the same ingress controller or proxy instance by listing Ingress and HTTPRoute objects grouped by ingress class or gateway reference.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq 'group_by(.metadata.annotations["kubernetes.io/ingress.class"] // .spec.ingressClassName) | .[] | {ingressClass: .[0].metadata.annotations["kubernetes.io/ingress.class"] // .[0].spec.ingressClassName, namespaces: [.[].metadata.namespace] | unique}'; kubectl get httproute -A -o json | jq '[.items[] | {namespace: .metadata.namespace, parentRefs: .spec.parentRefs}] | group_by(.parentRefs[].name)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Groups showing multiple distinct namespaces routing through the same ingress class or gateway name indicate shared proxy scope across trust boundaries.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the proxy pod's routing configuration to determine whether it has backend pools or upstream clusters from namespaces classified under different security zones or tenant labels.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get pods -n ingress-nginx -o wide; kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-upstream"] != null) | {namespace: .metadata.namespace, securityZone: .metadata.labels["security-zone"]}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Services with differing security-zone label values being routed through the same proxy instance confirms shared_across_trust_boundaries scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the ingress controller or API gateway deployment manifest to determine if namespace selectors or security zone labels are used to isolate proxy instances per trust boundary.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get deployment -n ingress-nginx ingress-nginx-controller -o yaml | grep -E 'namespaces:|watchNamespace:|--watch-namespace'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: '--watch-namespace=<single-namespace>' or equivalent namespace restriction flag confirms the proxy is scoped to a single trust boundary. Absence of namespace restriction means the proxy serves all namespaces (shared).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the platform team to obtain the proxy deployment topology diagram and confirm whether separate proxy instances are provisioned per security zone (PCI, production, staging, tenant A/B) or whether a single shared ingress tier handles all zones.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Architecture documentation showing one ingress controller deployment per security classification zone with no cross-zone backend routing confirms single_trust_boundary scope.

typical_values: shared_across_trust_boundaries (most common in cost-optimized deployments with a single shared NGINX ingress)
single_trust_boundary (security-hardened environments with dedicated ingress per namespace or zone)
unknown (environments where proxy topology has not been inventoried or documented)

option_description: Specifies the application protocol used by the proxy to communicate with the backend destination service after performing TLS termination on the client-facing side. Determines whether the proxy-to-backend segment is encrypted (https, grpcs, tcp_tls) or plaintext (http, grpc, tcp_plaintext), which directly controls whether a decrypted transit segment exists within the cluster network.
security_impact: The Rego rule tls_termination_at_shared_proxy fires when backend_protocol is http, grpc, or tcp_plaintext, regardless of whether the proxy has a shared trust boundary scope. These plaintext values confirm that decrypted traffic traverses the internal network between proxy and backend, undermining end-to-end encrypted channel guarantees (T1573). An attacker with access to the cluster network, a compromised sidecar, or a rogue CNI plugin can intercept this plaintext segment. Even grpc (without TLS) is treated equivalently to http because gRPC over h2c provides no confidentiality. Only https, grpcs, and tcp_tls confirm re-encrypted backend communication.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query NGINX ingress backend-protocol annotations for all Ingress objects to identify which backends are configured for plaintext vs encrypted protocols.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, backendProtocol: (.metadata.annotations["nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol"] // "HTTP (default, plaintext)"), serviceName: .spec.rules[].http.paths[].backend.service.name}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Entries showing 'HTTPS' or 'GRPCS' are secure. Entries showing 'HTTP', 'GRPC', or the default unset value confirm plaintext backend_protocol.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Envoy sidecar or gateway upstream cluster definitions via the admin API to identify the transport protocol and TLS context for each upstream.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl exec -n <namespace> <envoy-proxy-pod> -- curl -s localhost:15000/clusters | grep -E 'tls_context|transport_socket|grpc|http' | head -40; kubectl exec -n istio-system deploy/istio-ingressgateway -- curl -s localhost:15000/config_dump | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(c['cluster']['name'], c['cluster'].get('transport_socket',{}).get('@type','NO_TLS')) for c in d.get('configs',[])[3].get('dynamic_active_clusters',[])]"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Clusters showing 'envoy.transport_sockets.tls' type confirm TLS upstream (https/grpcs/tcp_tls). Clusters with 'NO_TLS' or no transport socket entry confirm plaintext backend protocol.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Traefik IngressRoute or service router configuration files for protocol scheme definitions on backend service URLs.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get ingressroute -A -o yaml | grep -E 'url:|scheme:|loadBalancer:|serversTransport:'; kubectl get serverstransport -A -o yaml | grep -E 'insecureSkipVerify:|rootCAs:|serverName:'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Service URLs beginning with 'https://' or 'grpcs://' and ServersTransport objects with rootCAs configured confirm encrypted backend protocol. 'http://' or 'grpc://' URLs confirm plaintext.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use a network sniffer on the pod network namespace of the proxy to observe whether backend-bound traffic contains TLS Client Hello records or cleartext HTTP headers.
how_to_obtain.command: POD=$(kubectl get pod -n ingress-nginx -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'); kubectl exec -n ingress-nginx $POD -- sh -c 'apk add tcpdump -q && tcpdump -i eth0 -A -n port 443 or port 80 or port 8080 -c 50 2>/dev/null' | grep -E 'GET |POST |HTTP/|TLSv|ClientHello'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS version strings and ClientHello records confirm encrypted backend communication (https/grpcs/tcp_tls). Plaintext HTTP method verbs (GET, POST) or HTTP version strings confirm plaintext backend_protocol (http/grpc/tcp_plaintext).

typical_values: http (most common default; NGINX ingress forwards to ClusterIP services over HTTP)
https (used in hardened deployments with backend TLS termination at service pods)
grpc (common in gRPC microservice environments without mesh-enforced mTLS)
grpcs (used in gRPC environments with explicit TLS configured on backend services)
tcp_tls (encrypted TCP stream proxying, less common)
